newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 9.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- Japan seized a Korean fishing boat on Tuesday, the fifth in a month for violating its terriorial waters.
- Union and management negotiators of the Seoul Metropolitan Subway Corp continued bargaining early into the morning today to avert a threatened strike.

- The ruling New Korea Party's largest faction, the Council for Political Development is heading toward a split over differences between members over whom to support in the party's presidential nomination race.

- The visiting Russian deputy prime minister said that Korean companies setting up plants or other facilities at an industrial complex to be built in the Nakhodka free trade zone will receive a number of tax breaks.

- The total amount of debt owed by local firms to financial institutions stood at 797.4 trillion won at the end of March this year, up 6 percent from the 750.3 trillion won recorded at the end of 1996.
- The business sector recently has gone on high alert over the possible spread of labour strikes at major companies across the nation.
